title: Microfluidic Digital Logic Chip Assembly
author: Erik Werner
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8efhtbn
materials: When the materials are close, press firmly from the center outwards to adhere all layers together.
Clamp with binder clips on all four sides.

steps.title: Clean Device Components
steps.instruction: Rinse all parts to be assembled under a stream of DI water to remove charred material or debris from machining.

steps.title: Sonicate Components
steps.instruction: Clean components using a sonicator (Branson, B2510) with a soap solution.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a solution of ~1% Microsoap (or liquid dish soap) in DI water.
Insert each component of the Microfluidic device into a 3" x 4" zip loc bag, filling the bag about halfway with the solution.
If parts only have features on one side, combine two pieces in one bag with non-patterned surfaces facing each other.
Sonicate the bags for 20 minutes.
Remove parts from bags, rinse thoroughly with DI water, and dry with compressed nitrogen.
Transfer parts to a Petri dish to maintain cleanliness.

steps.title: Prepare Bottom PMMA Layer
steps.instruction: Prepare the bottom layer of the device in a laminar flow hood (Envirco, TT4830).

substeps.instruction: Insert four tapered dowel pins into a PMMA piece (this becomes the 'bottom' layer), ensuring the small end of the pin faces the side with the features to be bonded.
Orient the chip features face up and inspect for dust/debris using a stereoscopic microscope (Olympus, SZ40).
Remove debris using compressed air or by lightly blotting with Scotch MagicTape (rolled into a 'wheel' to avoid residue).

steps.title: Bond PDMS Membrane to Bottom PMMA
steps.instruction: Align and adhere the PDMS membrane to the bottom PMMA layer.

substeps.instruction: Orient the PDMS membrane over the PMMA layer and peel away the PET layer protecting the side that contacts the PMMA.
Clean the exposed PDMS thoroughly with MagicTape to remove dust.
Using the tapered dowel pins, lower the PDMS onto the PMMA chip.
Press the middle of the PDMS to start adhesion, allowing it to adhere from the middle outwards.
Remove one taper pin, crease the PDMS/PET at that corner, and peel off the top PET layer parallel to the device.
If the PDMS wrinkles or distorts, use the tapered dowel pins to realign and lower it onto the PMMA again.
Inspect for bubbles; if dust is found, peel back the PDMS and blot with MagicTape.

steps.title: Prepare Top PMMA Layer
steps.instruction: Clean and align the top PMMA layer onto the assembly.

substeps.instruction: Clean the exposed PDMS surface with MagicTape, securing at least two points of the membrane with a gloved finger to prevent lifting.
Reinsert the taper pins into the bottom PMMA/PDMS assembly.
Inspect and clean the top layer of PMMA using compressed air and MagicTape.
Lower the top PMMA layer, feature side down, over the taper pins onto the lower PMMA/PDMS assembly.
Remove the taper pins.

steps.title: Final Device Inspection and Cleaning
steps.instruction: Verify alignment and clean the exterior of the assembled chip.

substeps.instruction: Inspect the device to ensure features are aligned and no large air pockets exist.
Clean the outside of the device with compressed air and MagicTape to prevent imprints during annealing.

steps.title: Prepare Compression Bumpers
steps.instruction: Prepare PET/PDMS/PET bumpers to distribute pressure during compression.

substeps.instruction: Prepare two PET/PDMS/PET bumpers slightly larger than the device (at least 30mm extra length and width).
For the first bumper, crease one corner and peel away one PET layer parallel to the material.
Place the completed chip onto the exposed PDMS of the first bumper.
Peel one PET layer from the second bumper and place it on the opposite side of the chip.

steps.title: Assemble Compression Sandwich
steps.instruction: Sandwich the assembly between rigid slides for annealing.

substeps.instruction: Sandwich the chip and bumpers between glass slides (or aluminum plates), ensuring the entire device is covered.
Verify the stack order from top to bottom: Glass, PET, PDMS, PMMA, PDMS, PMMA, PDMS, PET, Glass.
Trim away excess PDMS/PET bumper material, leaving a few mm of material sticking out.

steps.title: Anneal the Device
steps.instruction: Heat the assembly in an oven to complete lamination.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the assembly to an oven, setting the device vertically in the middle.
Heat to 110ºC and maintain the temperature thoroughly (for a 3mm device, heat for at least 2 hours).
If lamination is unsatisfactory, rebake in 1-hour increments or increase temperature in 1ºC increments.
Set the oven to room temperature and allow to cool completely (preferably overnight).

steps.title: Final Disassembly
steps.instruction: Remove compression materials to finalize the device.

substeps.instruction: Remove binder clips and glass slides.
Peel away the outer PET/PDMS bumpers (these may be left in place if the device is not for immediate use to protect from dust).
